one_line: Guru Arjan, fifth Sikh Guru and compiler of the Adi Granth, working with his scribe Bhai Gurdas in early 17th‑century Punjab.

appearance.age_look: Guru Arjan appears in his late 30s with a calm, medium build; Bhai Gurdas appears in his early 40s, slightly broader and sturdy.
appearance.face: Guru Arjan has an oval face, warm wheatish complexion, neatly combed medium-length beard and moustache, soft but resolute eyes with slightly arched brows, and a serene, gentle default expression; Bhai Gurdas has a slightly squarer face, similar wheatish tone, fuller neatly groomed beard, strong nose and jaw, with an alert, focused default expression.
appearance.hair: Both wear their hair tied in a topknot concealed under distinct turbans: Guru Arjan’s is a smooth, slightly rounded white dastar wrapped close to the head with no ornament; Bhai Gurdas wears a deep indigo, slightly taller dastar with subtle wrap folds, also without decoration.
appearance.costume: Guru Arjan wears a long, ankle-length off‑white cotton jama (Mughal‑era robe) with a simple round collar and straight sleeves, tied with a soft pale‑gold patka sash at the waist, over loose white churidar trousers and plain brown leather jutti shoes; over this he has a light, unpatterned cream muslin chadar draped around shoulders and forearms in a modest, enveloping way, giving him a luminous, ascetic look; Bhai Gurdas wears a knee‑length light‑blue cotton angarkha with a wrapped front tied at the side by narrow ties, over slightly darker blue loose salwar trousers gathered at the ankles, and dark brown leather jutti; he has a simple, functional dark‑brown leather manuscript belt pouch at his side, and a plain undyed cotton shawl draped over one shoulder for modesty and practicality; both are fully and modestly clothed with no bare torso or exposed legs.
appearance.signature: Guru Arjan’s signature prop is a large, carefully bound Adi Granth manuscript resting on a low wooden manjhi (reading stand) that he gently steadies with one hand, its thick handmade paper pages edged in a warm buff tone; Bhai Gurdas’s signature prop is a long reed pen held in his right hand and a small wooden ink pot and narrow palm‑leaf style writing board in his left, showing him actively scribing beside the manuscript.

ref_desc: Guru Arjan, in an off‑white jama with cream chadar, white dastar and brown jutti, gently steadies a large Adi Granth manuscript on a wooden stand beside Bhai Gurdas in light‑blue angarkha, deep indigo dastar and brown jutti holding a reed pen, ink pot and writing board.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character pair of Guru Arjan and Bhai Gurdas as a consistent model sheet in early 17th‑century Mughal Punjab: Guru Arjan appears as a serene, medium‑built man in his late 30s with an oval face, wheatish complexion, neatly combed medium‑length beard and moustache, soft but resolute eyes and a calm expression, his hair tied in a hidden topknot under a smooth, rounded white dastar; he wears a long ankle‑length off‑white cotton jama with a simple round collar and straight sleeves, tied with a pale‑gold sash at the waist, over loose white churidar trousers and plain brown leather jutti, with a light cream muslin chadar modestly draped around his shoulders and forearms, and he gently steadies a large, thick, buff‑edged Adi Granth manuscript resting on a low wooden reading stand. Beside him, Bhai Gurdas appears as a slightly broader man in his early 40s with a squarer face, wheatish skin, fuller neatly groomed beard, strong features and an alert, focused expression, his hair knotted under a deep indigo, slightly taller dastar; he wears a knee‑length light‑blue cotton angarkha wrapped and tied at the side, over darker blue loose salwar trousers gathered at the ankles, dark brown leather jutti, a simple dark‑brown leather belt pouch and an undyed cotton shawl over one shoulder, holding in his hands a long reed pen, a small wooden ink pot and a narrow writing board to show his role as scribe; use a soft palette of off‑white, cream, pale gold, deep indigo, light blue and brown leather tones, and present them front‑facing and three‑quarter views in one image so their face shapes, turbans, robes, shawls, footwear and scholarly props are clear and repeatable.
